taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-15): "a leafy flowering stalk that may be up to 6 feet (15 dm) tall with numerous small white flowers".

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), its top held to the 1.5 m FEIS gives as the most (Crane 1990).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it; FEIS calls the leaves linear, tough and wiry (Crane 1990).

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-15): "a perennial, evergreen herb".

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: A model estimate (confidence high): alternate leaves, crowded at the base and smaller up the stalk, as FEIS's "basal leaves that form dense clumps" and "leafy flowering stalk" (Crane 1990) leave the arrangement unsaid.

traits.rosette.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-15): "basal leaves that form dense clumps or tussocks".

traits.perennation.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-15): the leaves "arise from a short, woody rhizome"; it reproduces by offshoots of the rhizome.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high): a raceme, a dense cluster that blooms from the lowest flowers up, leaving a knob of buds on top (FEIS, Crane 1990).

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-15): "The fruit is a small three-lobed capsule containing several seeds".

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's common beargrass review (Crane 1990, read 2026-10-16): in Washington fruits green on August 27, half brown by September 10, opening and shedding seed by September 25, all open on October 10; read as September and October.

generator.params.note: Pacific trillium's program values, changed by hand for beargrass: a dense clump of 24 long, arching, wiry basal leaves, and flowering stalks with four long leaves up them ending in a long dense raceme of small white flowers that opens from the bottom up (FEIS, Crane 1990). A clump blooms only some years (FEIS: colonies bloom in 5- to 7-year cycles), so drawn, a little over half of adult stalks flower. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.1 m to the top of the flowering stalk at 8 years, below the 1.5 m FEIS gives as the most (Crane 1990). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey-green wiry leaves; creamy white flowers.

traits.life_span.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L291495), as no source read gives it.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L291495), as no source read gives it.

traits.sexual_system.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L291495), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L291495), as no source read gives it.
